svg.title: Odometry: adding up wheel motion into a position
svg.desc: Animated. A field seen from above with WPILib's directions in the corner: x is forward, y is left, and counter-clockwise turns are positive. A robot drives a curve, turning left. A dashed blue outline, where odometry thinks the robot is, follows it, leaving a trail of blue dots as the code adds up each wheel's motion and the gyro's heading every 20 ms. Partway along, a wheel slips: the robot hardly moves but the estimate keeps going, counting ground the robot never covered. By the end the estimate is ahead of the real robot: errors add up. Then a camera sees an AprilTag on the wall and the estimate jumps back onto the robot. Below: a wheel 2% smaller than the code thinks makes every distance 2% short, and a slipping wheel counts ground it never covered.
svg.text: Odometry: adding up wheel motion into a position
Wheel motion and gyro heading, added up into where the robot thinks it is.
a wheel slips: it counts ground
Every 20 ms the code adds each module's wheel turns × wheel size, at its
angle, plus the gyro's heading. A wheel 2% smaller than the code thinks
makes every distance 2% short, and a slipping wheel counts ground it
